author: propertylenden
author_bio: Now Real Estate Consultant. Still evolving.
text:
One thing I feel missing from discussion around yesterday’s rain in Delhi & Gurgaon.
Delhi received heavy rainfall & Gurgaon had heavy rainfall too. But when I searched online, I found very few visuals from Delhi showing severe waterlogging.
 In contrast social media flooded with videos from Gurgaon showing roads submerged, cars stuck & infrastructure failures.
This is where administration and execution make a difference.
I have personally witnessed  work done in Delhi over the last 6 to 12 months: large scale desilting, drainage upgrades n replacement of smaller pipes with bigger drainage lines in several areas. This impact was visible yesterday.
A year or two ago Delhi used to face situations very similar to Gurgaon during heavy rains. So this is not about claiming Delhi is perfect. Future rainfall may still create waterlogging in some areas. But if we talk specifically about yesterday contrast was noticeable.
I think Haryana’s authorities, especially in Gurgaon should learn what worked in Delhi and implement similar measures. Gurgaon doesn't need excuses anymore. It needs execution.

text:
Heavy Rain Brings Delhi Traffic to a Standstill, Zakhira Underpass Flooded

Heavy rain in Delhi led to waterlogging and traffic disruptions across several areas. Several feet of water accumulated at Zakhira Underpass, leaving multiple vehicles stranded.

Traffic movement on both sides of the underpass was affected due to the waterlogging.

The situation has once again raised questions over Delhi’s drainage system and the administration’s preparedness to deal with heavy rainfall.
